title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 25 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Chronicles chapter 25 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 25 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Chronicles Chapter 25.

questions.question: In 2 Chronicles 25, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Amaziah was twenty and five years old when he began to reign
Amaziah gathered Judah together and made captains over thousands
He hired an hundred thousand mighty men of valour out of Israel
A man of God came to Amaziah and warned him not to let the army of Israel go with him
questions.correctAnswer: Amaziah was twenty and five years old when he began to reign
questions.explanation: This event is described in 2 Chronicles 25:1, which is the first verse of the chapter.

questions.question: How old was Amaziah when he began to reign?
questions.correctAnswer: Twenty and five years old
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 25:1 states that Amaziah was twenty and five years old when he began to reign.

questions.question: What is the name of Amaziah's mother?
questions.correctAnswer: Jehoaddan
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 25:1 states that Amaziah's mother's name was Jehoaddan of Jerusalem.

questions.question: How is Amaziah's conduct described before the LORD?
options: He did that which was right but not with a perfect heart
He did evil in the sight of the LORD
He did that which was right with a perfect heart
He was wicked throughout his reign
questions.correctAnswer: He did that which was right but not with a perfect heart
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 25:2 says Amaziah did that which was right in the sight of the LORD, but not with a perfect heart.

questions.question: What did Amaziah do to the servants who killed his father?
questions.correctAnswer: He slew them
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 25:3 states that Amaziah slew his servants who had killed the king his father.

questions.question: Did Amaziah kill the children of those servants who killed his father?
options: No, he did not kill their children
questions.correctAnswer: No, he did not kill their children
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 25:4 states that he slew not their children, following the law in the book of Moses.

questions.question: How many choice men able to go forth to war did Amaziah find in Judah and Benjamin?
questions.correctAnswer: Three hundred thousand
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 25:5 reports that Amaziah numbered three hundred thousand choice men able to go forth to war.

questions.question: How many mighty men of valour did Amaziah hire out of Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: One hundred thousand
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 25:6 says Amaziah hired an hundred thousand mighty men of valour out of Israel.

questions.question: What did the man of God warn Amaziah about the army of Israel?
options: Let not the army of Israel go with thee, for the LORD is not with Israel
The army of Israel will bring victory
The army of Israel should lead the battle
The army of Israel will be loyal to you
questions.correctAnswer: Let not the army of Israel go with thee, for the LORD is not with Israel
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 25:7 records the man of God warning Amaziah not to let the army of Israel go with him because the LORD is not with Israel.

questions.question: How did Amaziah respond to the man of God's warning about the payment to the army of Israel?
options: He asked what they should do for the hundred talents given
He immediately sent the army away without comment
questions.correctAnswer: He asked what they should do for the hundred talents given
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 25:9 states Amaziah asked the man of God what they should do for the hundred talents he had given to the army of Israel.

questions.question: What was the reaction of the army of Israel when Amaziah sent them home?
options: Their anger was greatly kindled against Judah
They made a treaty with Amaziah
questions.correctAnswer: Their anger was greatly kindled against Judah
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 25:10 says that the army's anger was greatly kindled against Judah and they returned home in great anger.

questions.question: Amaziah made captains over thousands and hundreds according to the houses of their fathers throughout Judah and Benjamin.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 25:5 states that Amaziah gathered Judah together and made captains over thousands and hundreds according to the houses of their fathers throughout Judah and Benjamin.

questions.question: The LORD commanded that the fathers shall not die for the children, neither shall the children die for the fathers, but every man shall die for his own sin.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 25:4 quotes the law in the book of Moses stating that the fathers shall not die for the children, nor the children for the fathers.

questions.question: Amaziah reigned for forty years in Jerusalem.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 25:1 states that Amaziah reigned twenty and nine years, not forty.

questions.question: The man of God told Amaziah that the LORD would help the army of Israel against their enemies.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 25:7 states the LORD is not with Israel, and the man of God warned Amaziah not to take the army of Israel with him.

medium.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 25 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Chronicles Chapter 25 to real-life situations.

questions.question: How many children of Seir did Amaziah smite in the valley of salt?
questions.correctAnswer: Ten thousand
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 25:11 states that Amaziah smote ten thousand children of Seir in the valley of salt.

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 25:12 promise will happen if someone casts enemies down from the top of a rock as Amaziah did?
options: They all will be broken in pieces
They will be taken as slaves
questions.correctAnswer: They all will be broken in pieces
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 25:12 explains that the children of Judah cast the captives down from the top of the rock so that they all were broken in pieces.

questions.question: What was the consequence for the cities of Judah after Amaziah sent back the soldiers he hired from Israel?
options: Three thousand were slain and much spoil was taken
The cities were fortified and safe
questions.correctAnswer: Three thousand were slain and much spoil was taken
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 25:13 shows that the soldiers sent back from Israel fell upon the cities of Judah and smote three thousand of them, taking much spoil.

questions.question: How did Amaziah's worship of the gods of Seir affect his relationship with the LORD, according to 2 Chronicles 25:14–15?
options: The LORD's anger was kindled against him and He sent a prophet to rebuke him
The LORD punished the children of Seir instead
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD's anger was kindled against him and He sent a prophet to rebuke him
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 25:14–15 explains that after Amaziah bowed down to the gods of Seir, the LORD's anger was kindled against him and He sent a prophet to question his idolatry.

questions.question: What practical lesson can be learned from Amaziah's refusal to listen to the prophet's counsel about the gods of Edom?
options: Ignoring godly counsel can lead to destruction
questions.correctAnswer: Ignoring godly counsel can lead to destruction
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 25:16 states that because Amaziah did not heed the prophet's counsel, God had determined to destroy him, showing the importance of obedience and listening to godly advice.

questions.question: What was Joash king of Israel's warning to Amaziah in 2 Chronicles 25:18–19?
options: Do not boast and meddle lest you fall
questions.correctAnswer: Do not boast and meddle lest you fall
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 25:18–19 records Joash warning Amaziah not to be proud over his victory and to avoid meddling in matters that would lead to his downfall.

questions.question: What was the reason given in 2 Chronicles 25:20 for Amaziah's downfall?
options: Because he sought after the gods of Edom
Because he trusted in the LORD alone
Because he listened to the prophet
questions.correctAnswer: Because he sought after the gods of Edom
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 25:20 explains Amaziah's refusal to listen was allowed by God so that Amaziah would fall due to his idolatry with the gods of Edom.

questions.question: Why did Amaziah send back the hundred thousand mighty men of valor from Israel, according to 2 Chronicles 25:7–10?
options: Because a man of God told him the LORD was not with Israel
Because he could not pay them
Because they were defeated in battle
questions.correctAnswer: Because a man of God told him the LORD was not with Israel
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 25:7–10 show that a man of God warned Amaziah not to bring Israel's army, so he sent them back despite their anger.

questions.question: What does Amaziah's initial action of strengthening himself and organizing captains over thousands and hundreds teach about leadership in 2 Chronicles 25:5?
options: Effective leadership requires preparation and organization
Leadership is solely about personal strength
questions.correctAnswer: Effective leadership requires preparation and organization
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 25:5 describes Amaziah gathering captains and numbering men for war, illustrating the importance of preparation and structure in leadership.

questions.question: What does the story of Amaziah casting the captives down from the rock in 2 Chronicles 25:12 teach about mercy and consequences in warfare?
options: Harsh treatment of captives can reflect a hardened heart
Mercy is always shown in war
questions.correctAnswer: Harsh treatment of captives can reflect a hardened heart
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 25:12 shows that Amaziah's forces cast captives down to their death, indicating a lack of mercy and a ruthless approach, which has spiritual implications.

questions.question: How can the interaction between Amaziah and the prophet in 2 Chronicles 25:15–16 inform believers about responding to correction?
options: Rejecting correction can lead to destruction
Prophets should not speak to kings
Correction is unnecessary for the righteous
questions.correctAnswer: Rejecting correction can lead to destruction
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 25:15–16 shows Amaziah refusing the prophet's warning, which led to God's judgment, teaching the importance of humility and openness to correction.

questions.question: What does Joash's metaphor of the thistle and cedar in 2 Chronicles 25:18 imply about pride and humility?
options: Pride leads to downfall when faced with greater strength
The thistle is stronger than the cedar
questions.correctAnswer: Pride leads to downfall when faced with greater strength
questions.explanation: Joash's metaphor in 2 Chronicles 25:18 warns that the small thistle boasting to the mighty cedar is foolish, illustrating that pride without strength invites destruction.

questions.question: What lesson about faithfulness can be drawn from Amaziah doing right but not with a perfect heart in 2 Chronicles 25:2?
options: Partial obedience is insufficient for full blessing
Doing right is enough regardless of heart
questions.correctAnswer: Partial obedience is insufficient for full blessing
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 25:2 indicates Amaziah did right but not perfectly, showing that incomplete faithfulness can limit God's favor and lead to problems.

questions.question: True or False: Amaziah took advice and sent to Joash king of Israel to see one another face to face before the battle.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 25:17 says Amaziah took advice and sent to Joash king of Israel, suggesting a meeting face to face.

questions.question: True or False: Amaziah obeyed the prophet and abandoned his idols before the battle.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 25:16 shows Amaziah refusing the prophet's counsel and 25:20 explains his downfall was because he sought the gods of Edom, indicating disobedience.

hard.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 25 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Chronicles Chapter 25.

questions.question: Where did Joash king of Israel and Amaziah king of Judah meet face to face?
questions.correctAnswer: Bethshemesh
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 25:21 states that Joash and Amaziah saw one another in the face at Bethshemesh.

questions.question: What was the outcome of the battle between Judah and Israel at Bethshemesh?
options: Judah was put to the worse
questions.correctAnswer: Judah was put to the worse
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 25:22 explains that Judah was defeated and fled every man to his tent.

questions.question: What significant action did Joash king of Israel take after capturing Amaziah?
options: Broke down the wall of Jerusalem
Took Amaziah as a hostage to Lachish
questions.correctAnswer: Broke down the wall of Jerusalem
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 25:23 records that Joash broke down the wall of Jerusalem from the gate of Ephraim to the corner gate.

questions.question: What treasures did Joash take from Jerusalem after defeating Amaziah?
options: Gold, silver, vessels from the house of God, treasures of the king's house, and hostages
Only the vessels from the house of God
questions.correctAnswer: Gold, silver, vessels from the house of God, treasures of the king's house, and hostages
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 25:24 details that Joash took all gold, silver, vessels from the house of God, treasures of the king's house, and hostages.

questions.question: How many years did Amaziah live after the death of Joash king of Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: Fifteen years
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 25:25 states that Amaziah lived fifteen years after the death of Joash king of Israel.

questions.question: What eventually happened to Amaziah after he turned away from following the LORD?
options: A conspiracy was made against him and he was killed at Lachish
He died of natural causes in Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: A conspiracy was made against him and he was killed at Lachish
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 25:27 records that after turning away from the LORD, a conspiracy was made against Amaziah, and he was slain at Lachish.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'chereb' in 2 Chronicles 25:11 mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Sword
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'chereb' (חרב) commonly means 'sword' and is used in 2 Chronicles 25:11 to denote the weapon used by soldiers.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in 2 Chronicles 25:18 with the comparison of the thistle and the cedar?
questions.correctAnswer: Metaphor
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 25:18 uses metaphor by comparing the thistle and cedar to represent the relationship between Amaziah and Joash.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of divine judgment for idolatry found in 2 Chronicles 25:14-15?
questions.correctAnswer: Romans 1:18-32
questions.explanation: Romans 1:18-32 discusses God's wrath against idolatry, paralleling the judgment against Amaziah for worshipping Edomite gods in 2 Chronicles 25:14-15.

questions.question: Which Old Testament verse foreshadows the consequences experienced by Amaziah for turning to foreign gods as in 2 Chronicles 25:27?
questions.correctAnswer: Deuteronomy 28:15
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 28:15 warns of curses and destruction for disobedience, foreshadowing Amaziah’s downfall after turning from the LORD in 2 Chronicles 25:27.

questions.question: What event immediately precedes Joash breaking down the wall of Jerusalem in 2 Chronicles 25:23?
options: The defeat of Judah before Israel at Bethshemesh
Joash’s sending a prophet to Amaziah
questions.correctAnswer: The defeat of Judah before Israel at Bethshemesh
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 25:22 records Judah's defeat at Bethshemesh immediately before Joash breaks down Jerusalem’s wall in verse 23.

questions.question: Which Hebrew literary device is illustrated by the sequence of Amaziah hiring Israelite soldiers and then sending them away in 2 Chronicles 25:6-10?
questions.correctAnswer: Irony
questions.explanation: The irony lies in Amaziah hiring Israelite soldiers to fight but then sending them away, which leads to their anger and subsequent attack on Judah (2 Chronicles 25:6-10).

questions.question: How does Amaziah’s action of setting up the gods of Seir after the Edomite slaughter illustrate a typology in 2 Chronicles 25:14?
options: It typifies apostasy following military success
It typifies the role of prophets
questions.correctAnswer: It typifies apostasy following military success
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 25:14 shows Amaziah’s apostasy by worshipping Edomite gods after victory, a typology of falling away after success.

questions.question: True or False: Joash returned all the treasures he took from Jerusalem to Amaziah after the battle.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 25:24 states Joash took the treasures and returned to Samaria, not giving anything back to Amaziah.

questions.question: True or False: Amaziah’s reign was characterized by perfect faithfulness to the LORD according to 2 Chronicles 25:2.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 25:2 explicitly states Amaziah did right in the sight of the LORD but not with a perfect heart.

theological.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 25 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Chronicles Chapter 25 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Chronicles 25:4 teach about individual responsibility for sin?
options: Each person bears their own guilt and punishment for sin
Children inherit the sins and punishment of their fathers
Kings are exempt from punishment for their servants' sins
Communal guilt extends to all descendants in a family
questions.correctAnswer: Each person bears their own guilt and punishment for sin
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 25:4 states that 'The fathers shall not die for the children, neither shall the children die for the fathers, but every man shall die for his own sin,' teaching individual responsibility for sin.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine judgment and human pride is taught in 2 Chronicles 25:19?
options: Boasting after victory can lead to downfall by divine judgment
God rewards the proud who trust in their own strength
Human pride is virtuous when justified by success
Victory guarantees divine approval regardless of attitude
questions.correctAnswer: Boasting after victory can lead to downfall by divine judgment
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 25:19 warns Amaziah against pride after victory, implying that such boasting leads to ruin, showing God's judgment on pride.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning incomplete obedience does 2 Chronicles 25:2 reveal about human sanctification?
options: Doing right but not with a perfect heart demonstrates partial sanctification
Complete sanctification is achievable through human effort
External obedience suffices for full righteousness before God
Sinless perfection is expected at the start of reigns
questions.correctAnswer: Doing right but not with a perfect heart demonstrates partial sanctification
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 25:2 states Amaziah 'did that which was right...but not with a perfect heart,' showing sanctification is a progressive, imperfect process.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Chronicles 25:8 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: Verse 8 states God has 'power to help, and to cast down,' illustrating divine sovereignty over human affairs and battle outcomes.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Chronicles 25:15 particularly highlight in God's dealings with Amaziah?
questions.correctAnswer: Justice
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 25:15 shows God's anger and sending a prophet to confront Amaziah for idolatry, reflecting God's justice.

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 25:11-12 connect with the broader biblical theme of divine judgment on enemies?
options: It exemplifies God's use of Israel as an instrument of judgment on nations
It contradicts the teaching of loving one's enemies
It shows human vengeance as superior to divine justice
It indicates that violence is always condemned in Scripture
questions.correctAnswer: It exemplifies God's use of Israel as an instrument of judgment on nations
questions.explanation: The victory over Edomites in verses 11-12 shows God empowering Israel to execute judgment, consistent with biblical themes of divine justice through His people.

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 25:14–15 foreshadow New Testament teachings on idolatry and apostasy?
options: They anticipate warnings against turning from God to false gods
They endorse syncretism as permissible worship
They show idolatry as a minor offense
They predict that idols can sometimes deliver people
questions.correctAnswer: They anticipate warnings against turning from God to false gods
questions.explanation: These verses illustrate the consequences of idolatry, prefiguring New Testament calls to remain faithful to God alone (cf. 1 Corinthians 10:14).

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 6 and 7 teach about reliance on human strength versus divine support?
options: Relying on human mercenaries is futile without God's blessing
Human military power guarantees victory apart from God
God supports those who rely on foreign armies
Hiring soldiers from another kingdom is a sign of faith
questions.correctAnswer: Relying on human mercenaries is futile without God's blessing
questions.explanation: Verse 6 shows Amaziah hiring Israelite soldiers; verse 7 contains a prophecy warning that God is not with Israel, indicating human strength apart from God is insufficient.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 24 and 27 teach about divine judgment and the consequences of apostasy for leadership?
options: Apostasy leads to political and personal ruin, including loss of wealth and life
Leaders who turn from God are always protected by their armies
Divine judgment on kings is delayed until after death
Material loss is unrelated to spiritual unfaithfulness
questions.correctAnswer: Apostasy leads to political and personal ruin, including loss of wealth and life
questions.explanation: Verse 24 describes Israel plundering Jerusalem after Amaziah's defeat; verse 27 records his assassination after turning from God, showing apostasy's consequences.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 4 and 27 teach about sin's consequences and divine justice in leadership contexts?
options: Leaders bear personal responsibility and divine justice for their sins
The sins of leaders are always forgiven without consequence
Children inherit the punishment for their parents' sins
Conspiracies against leaders are unrelated to divine judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Leaders bear personal responsibility and divine justice for their sins
questions.explanation: Verse 4 affirms individual responsibility for sin; verse 27 shows Amaziah's death after apostasy, illustrating divine justice upon leaders for their own sins.

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 25:10-13 teach in response to sceptics who claim God’s promises allow for disobedient alliances without consequence?
options: God’s presence is necessary for success; disobedient alliances provoke judgment
All alliances, regardless of obedience, bring victory
God ignores disobedient alliances if they involve payment
The text endorses use of any military help for success
questions.correctAnswer: God’s presence is necessary for success; disobedient alliances provoke judgment
questions.explanation: Verses 10-13 show that sending away the Israelite mercenaries led them to attack Judah’s cities, demonstrating danger of disobedient alliances and God’s absent blessing.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine sovereignty over human conflict is revealed in 2 Chronicles 25:22?
options: God determines the victor in battles according to His purpose
Human commanders alone decide battle outcomes
Victory is random and unrelated to divine will
Divine sovereignty is limited in earthly warfare
questions.correctAnswer: God determines the victor in battles according to His purpose
questions.explanation: Verse 22 states Judah was put to the worse before Israel, implying God’s sovereign control in determining outcomes of war.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is especially evident in 2 Chronicles 25:9 regarding God’s provision?
questions.correctAnswer: Providence
questions.explanation: Verse 9 records the man of God assuring Amaziah that God can provide much more than the silver paid, highlighting God’s providential care.

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 25:23-24 contribute to the theme of divine retribution in the biblical narrative?
options: It shows consequences of disobedience include loss of city defenses and wealth
It suggests divine retribution is always immediate and total
It denies any divine involvement in political defeats
It indicates that only foreign nations suffer divine retribution
questions.correctAnswer: It shows consequences of disobedience include loss of city defenses and wealth
questions.explanation: Verses 23-24 describe Joash breaking down Jerusalem’s wall and taking treasures, illustrating divine retribution on Judah due to Amaziah’s failures.

questions.question: What theological lesson about prophetic ministry does 2 Chronicles 25:16 teach?
options: Prophets faithfully declare God's judgment even if rejected by kings
Prophets always avoid confrontation with rulers
Prophets act only to comfort kings
Prophets can be dismissed without consequence
questions.correctAnswer: Prophets faithfully declare God's judgment even if rejected by kings
questions.explanation: Verse 16 shows the prophet warning Amaziah despite the king’s hostility, illustrating prophetic courage and obedience to God’s commission.
